newsitem.title: RUSSIA: IMF team arrives Russia on Monday to mull 97 plans.
newsitem.headline: IMF team arrives Russia on Monday to mull 97 plans.

text.p: A team of experts from the International Monetary Fund arrives in Moscow on Monday to finalise work on Russia's economic programme for 1997, IMF chief representative Martin Gilman said on Friday.
"The idea is to finalise the few remaining aspects of the 1997 programme so that it can be submitted for approval," Gilman told Reuters.
IMF teams visit Russia each month to assess economic performance and decide whether to recommend paying tranches of a $10 billion three-year loan to Russia.
IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus said during a visit to Russia earlier this month that he was ready to recommend the approval of the 1997 programme, which will underpin the loan.

Agreement on the 1997 programme could open the door to Russia receiving one or more tranches of the loan, postponed because the IMF is worried about low Russian tax revenues. The fund has so far not paid out any of the money due this year.

Russian officials have said the loan payments are less important to Moscow now than they were in past years because Russia has been raising funds on world capital markets with two Eurobonds, one denominated in dollars and one in marks.
A second dollar Eurobond is due later this year, although London dealers said on Thursday that it would not come before June as the market waited for sentiment to improve.
